JD Sports Fashion Lowers Profit Target After Sales Fall
JD Sports Fashion trimmed its profit target for the current fiscal year after it reported lower sales for the third quarter ahead of the key festive period.

The U.K. sneaker and fashion retailer now expects profit before tax and adjusted items--a company-preferred metric--to be in a range of 700 million pounds to 750 million pounds ($920.6 million-$986.3 million), down from a previous forecast of between 700 million pounds and 800 million pounds.

The group booked sales of 2.91 billion pounds for its third quarter through October, 1.1% lower organically compared with the same period a year prior. On a like-for-like basis, sales dropped 2.6% on year.
"At group level, trading in the quarter was in line with our expectations," Chief Executive Regis Schultz said.
